title_orig: A Dialogue of Comfort against Tribulation
title_es: Diálogo de consuelo contra la tribulación
title_en: A Dialogue of Comfort against Tribulation
date: c. 1534 (composed in the Tower; first printed 1553 by Tottel, per the Dent introduction)
genre: Dialogue (Anthony and Vincent, Hungarian uncle and nephew)
edition_original: Dent 1913 (Everyman), 'Utopia with the Dialogue of Comfort', Dialogue reprinted from the 16th-century text with contractions expanded (editor's note, p. xxxvi-xxxvii); read as archive.org item utopiawiththedia00moreuoft, page images n163 (p.128) and n164 (p.129)
edition_english: Same text (the English is original); modernised public-domain edition: Monica Stevens, 'Dialogue of Comfort Against Tribulation, with modifications to obsolete language' (Project Gutenberg #17075), used for quote_en
licence: Dent 1913 (US public domain by date; the 16th-century text is public domain). Project Gutenberg #17075: 'Public domain in the USA' per its licence text. CCEL pages: not checked for licence. 1557 Workes (archive.org thomasmoreworkes) also read as OCR only: contains 'Mahomettes lawe' and 'Machometanes' in other works.
authenticity_note: Authentic (More's own Dialogue, 1534). The Dent text is the same sixteenth-century wording as the 1557 Workes (OCR there reads 'Mahomettes lawe'), but Dent's text is an edited reprint with some change of contractions.
notes: Mahomet occurs in the Book One introductory dialogue (Vincent's fear of Turkish conquest), in the Book Three introductory dialogue (the Turk's oath to dilate Mahomet's faith; forced conversion; 'ungracious sect of Mahomet'), and in Book Three ch. XIV (a hypothetical lord who would grant Mahomet as a true prophet). In CCEL Book II chapters I-XX (checked as HTML text) 'Mahomet' does not occur; 'Turk' does (chs. X and XII). The Gutenberg/CCEL texts are modernised, so use Dent for the 16th-century wording. Not checked: Book Two chs. XV-XVII in Dent for further Mahomet mentions.

title_orig: The Workes of Sir Thomas More Knyght (1557) - Dialogue concerning Heresies, Supplication of Souls, Confutation of Tyndale's Answer (location only)
title_es: Obras de Tomás Moro (1557), edición de 1557
title_en: The Workes of Sir Thomas More Knyght (1557)
licence: Public domain (1557 print); scanner notice not checked.
authenticity_note: Genuine More works. Here used only to locate passages; black-letter OCR is too unreliable to quote verbatim.
notes: Located but NOT quoted: 'Machomet' (seven-years sect, Lutheran comparison) and 'Machomettes doctrine', 'Machometanes' in the Dialogue concerning Heresies / Confutation area (OCR lines ~50439-50461, ~85269, ~87266); I could not confirm the page for the Lutheran comparison in the facsimile (checked pages 310-318 and 'The fourth boke' pages; not found). Also a Janissary/Mamluk passage (p. 279 area, ch. XV of Book IV) reads 'Mammelukes or Geniseries about the Turke and Sowda, have used to christen their children of purpose' in OCR - image was readable at 800px, not quoted. The Dialogue of Comfort itself appears in the 1557 OCR (line ~219611: 'stande wyth Mahomettes lawe').

title_orig: De veritate fidei christianae libri V
title_es: De la verdad de la fe cristiana (cinco libros)
title_en: On the Truth of the Christian Faith (five books)
genre: Apologetic treatise in five books; Book IV is a dialogue Christianus / Alfaquinus 'contra sectam Mahumetis'
edition_original: Basel: Oporinus, 1544 (title page: 'De veritate fidei christianae libri V ... contra Ethnicos, Iudaeos, Agarenos, siue Mahumetanos'), archive.org bim_early-english-books-1641-1700_joannes-lodus-viciv_1544. Google Books copy of the 1543 Basel edition (bub_gb_euXBdAALmykC) listed but not read.
edition_english: None found in public domain. Own translation used.
licence: Sixteenth-century print: public domain. Archive.org item metadata 'bim_early-english-books' (scan from a library digitisation); licence not checked.
authenticity_note: Genuine work by Vives. Book IV is written as a dialogue; the Muslim speaker (A L., 'Alfaquinus') is an interlocutor, and the Christian speaker (C H., 'Christianus') states the Islamic claims and refutes them.
notes: Book IV headings read: De Mahumete (p.574), De armis (p.576), 'Quod Christum conveniebat venire postremum' (p.586 area), De Alcorano, De corruptione Testamenti, De historiis Alcorani, De Deo, De Christo, De iis quibus persuasit sectam suam, De sociis eius, De legibus et vita Saracenorum, De die iudicii, De beatitudine. Only pp. 574-576 and 586 read as page images; other Book IV chapters read as OCR only. Book V not read.

title_es: De las discordias de Europa y de la república
title_en: On the Discords of Europe and the Commonwealth
genre: Political treatise / letter addressed to Adrian VI
edition_original: Google Books / archive.org copy bub_gb_76cPtBegErcC (OCR read)
notes: The OCR of this copy is too poor (Fraktur-like long-s errors) to quote verbatim. Chapters headed 'De bello Turcico' are a call to war (excluded, see excluded.json). The text mentions Turks and Mahumet in the context of Christian princes' disunity; not quoted.
